This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.\n\n## Ground your designs in the subject matter\n\nIf the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.\n\n## Design principles\n\nFor web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.\n\nTypography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.\n\nChoose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.\n\nDefault to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.\n\nAvoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:\n- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.\n- Using all caps for labels.\n- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.\n\nVisual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.\n\nUse non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.\n\nConsider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.\n\n## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique\n\nFor calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:\n1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);\n2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;\n3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;\n4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;\n5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.\n\nAll traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.\n\nWork in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.\n- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.\n- Type: the typefaces and their roles.\n- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?\n- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.\n\nThen review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.\n\nWhen writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.\n\n## Restraint and self-critique\n\nSpend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.\n\n## More on writing in design\n\nWords appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.\n\nWrite from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.\n\nUse active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: \"Save changes,\" not \"Submit.\" An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says \"Publish\" produces a toast that says \"Published.\" The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.\n\nTreat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. The nodes already extracted for those files are kept - they are still true - but the file is cached as partial and left unstamped in the manifest below, so the next `--update` re-dispatches it and replace-on-re-extract swaps the partial node set for a complete one. This is the same mechanism the library path uses for a truncated LLM response (#933, #1950), so both paths now recover instead of silently keeping a half-read file forever. A dispatched file with no coverage entry, or 0, was never opened, so whatever its chunk holds for it was guessed from its name: those items are dropped and the file is flagged the same way (#2225).\n\nMerge all chunk files into `.graphify_semantic_new.json`. **After each Agent call completes, read the real token counts from the Agent tool result's `usage` field and write them back into the chunk JSON before merging** — the chunk JSON itself always has placeholder zeros. Then run:\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json, glob\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nchunks = sorted(glob.glob('graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json'))\nall_nodes, all_edges, all_hyperedges = [], [], []\ntotal_in, total_out = 0, 0\nfor c in chunks:\n    d = json.loads(Path(c).read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\n    all_nodes += d.get('nodes', [])\n    all_edges += d.get('edges', [])\n    all_hyperedges += d.get('hyperedges', [])\n    total_in += d.get('input_tokens', 0)\n    total_out += d.get('output_tokens', 0)\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').write_text(json.dumps({\n    'nodes': all_nodes, 'edges': all_edges, 'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,\n    'input_tokens': total_in, 'output_tokens': total_out,\n}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nprint(f'Merged {len(chunks)} chunks: {total_in:,} in / {total_out:,} out tokens')\n\"\n```\n\nSave new results to cache. Pass the same SPEC_PATH as Step B0 — it stamps each entry with the prompt that produced it, and a write under a different prompt than the read lands where the next run won't look (#1939):\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom graphify.cache import save_semantic_cache\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nnew = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}\nuncached = [line for line in Path('graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\").splitlines() if line]\n# A partly-read file is cached with partial: True, which load_cached treats as a MISS,\n# so the next --update re-dispatches it instead of serving a truncated extraction forever\n# (#2225). Same contract the library path uses for a truncated LLM response (#933/#1950).\npartial = [line for line in Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\").splitlines() if line] if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').exists() else []\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\nsaved = save_semantic_cache(new.get('nodes', []), new.get('edges', []), new.get('hyperedges', []), root=INPUT_PATH, allowed_source_files=uncached, prompt_file='SPEC_PATH', partial_source_files=partial)\nnote = f' ({len(partial)} left partial for retry)' if partial else ''\nprint(f'Cached {saved} files' + note)\n\"\n```\n\nMerge cached + new results into `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json`:\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\ncached = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}\nnew = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}\n\nall_nodes = cached['nodes'] + new.get('nodes', [])\nall_edges = cached['edges'] + new.get('edges', [])\nall_hyperedges = cached.get('hyperedges', []) + new.get('hyperedges', [])\nseen = set()\ndeduped = []\nfor n in all_nodes:\n    if n['id'] not in seen:\n        seen.add(n['id'])\n        deduped.append(n)\n\nmerged = {\n    'nodes': deduped,\n    'edges': all_edges,\n    'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,\n    'input_tokens': new.get('input_tokens', 0),\n    'output_tokens': new.get('output_tokens', 0),\n}\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nprint(f'Extraction complete - {len(deduped)} nodes, {len(all_edges)} edges ({len(cached[\\\"nodes\\\"])} from cache, {len(new.get(\\\"nodes\\\",[]))} new)')\n\"\n```\nClean up temp files: `rm -f graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json`\n\n#### Part C - Merge AST + semantic into final extraction\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nast = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nsem = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\n\n# Stamp tier provenance on the semantic side. build._is_ast_tier reads\n# _origin when present and otherwise guesses from the SHAPE of\n# source_location ('L<line>' means AST). A subagent that writes 'L12' for a\n# doc section therefore made that node read as AST, and the next\n# graphify update deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it\n# seemed to belong to (#2843). extract() stamps its own items 'ast'; the\n# semantic side must say so explicitly.\nfor n in sem['nodes']:\n    n.setdefault('_origin', 'semantic')\nfor e in sem['edges']:\n    e.setdefault('_origin', 'semantic')\n\n# Merge: AST nodes first, semantic nodes deduplicated by id\nseen = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}\nmerged_nodes = list(ast['nodes'])\nfor n in sem['nodes']:\n    if n['id'] not in seen:\n        merged_nodes.append(n)\n        seen.add(n['id'])\n\nmerged_edges = ast['edges'] + sem['edges']\nmerged_hyperedges = sem.get('hyperedges', [])\nmerged = {\n    'nodes': merged_nodes,\n    'edges': merged_edges,\n    'hyperedges': merged_hyperedges,\n    'input_tokens': sem.get('input_tokens', 0),\n    'output_tokens': sem.get('output_tokens', 0),\n}\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\ntotal = len(merged_nodes)\nedges = len(merged_edges)\nprint(f'Merged: {total} nodes, {edges} edges ({len(ast[\\\"nodes\\\"])} AST + {len(sem[\\\"nodes\\\"])} semantic)')\n\"\n```\n\n### Step 4 - Build graph, cluster, analyze, generate outputs\n\n**Before starting:** the code blocks below pass `directed=IS_DIRECTED` to `build_from_json()` and `force=IS_FORCE` to `to_json()`. Replace `IS_DIRECTED` with `True` if `--directed` was given (builds a `DiGraph` preserving edge direction source→target), otherwise `False` (the default undirected `Graph`). Replace `IS_FORCE` with `True` if `--force` was given (permits intentional shrink, e.g. after deleting files), otherwise `False`. Substitute both so no literal `IS_DIRECTED` or `IS_FORCE` is left in the code. INPUT_PATH is not substituted — each block reads the scan root from the trusted `graphify-out/.graphify_root` that Step 1 resolved.\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p graphify-out\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfrom graphify.build import build_from_json\nfrom graphify.cluster import cluster, score_all\nfrom graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions\nfrom graphify.report import generate\nfrom graphify.export import to_json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nextraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\ndetection  = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\n\n# root= mirrors the --update runbook (#1361): relativize source_file to the same\n# base so the full build and incremental --update never drift apart on re-extract.\nG = build_from_json(extraction, root=INPUT_PATH, directed=IS_DIRECTED)\n# Guard BEFORE any write: an empty extraction must not clobber a good graph.json /\n# GRAPH_REPORT.md / analysis sidecar. Check immediately after build (#1392).\nif G.number_of_nodes() == 0:\n    print('ERROR: Graph is empty - extraction produced no nodes.')\n    print('Possible causes: all files were skipped, binary-only corpus, or extraction failed.')\n    raise SystemExit(1)\ncommunities = cluster(G)\ncohesion = score_all(G, communities)\ntokens = {'input': extraction.get('input_tokens', 0), 'output': extraction.get('output_tokens', 0)}\ngods = god_nodes(G)\nsurprises = surprising_connections(G, communities)\nlabels = {cid: 'Community ' + str(cid) for cid in communities}\n# Placeholder questions - regenerated with real labels in Step 5\nquestions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)\n\n# Export FIRST and honor the #479 shrink-guard: to_json returns False (writing\n# nothing) when the new graph is smaller than the existing graph.json. Only write\n# GRAPH_REPORT.md + the analysis sidecar when the graph was actually written, so\n# they never describe a graph that graph.json doesn't contain (#1392).\nwrote = to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json', force=IS_FORCE)\nif not wrote:\n    print('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json (existing graph has more nodes; #479).')\n    print('If this shrink is intentional (you deleted files), re-run a full build with --force.')\n    raise SystemExit(1)\nreport = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, gods, surprises, detection, tokens, INPUT_PATH, suggested_questions=questions)\nPath('graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nanalysis = {\n    'communities': {str(k): v for k, v in communities.items()},\n    'cohesion': {str(k): v for k, v in cohesion.items()},\n    'gods': gods,\n    'surprises': surprises,\n    'questions': questions,\n}\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json').write_text(json.dumps(analysis, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nprint(f'Graph: {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {G.number_of_edges()} edges, {len(communities)} communities')\n\"\n```\n\nIf this step prints `ERROR: Graph is empty`, stop and tell the user what happened - do not proceed to labeling or visualization.\n\nINPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root`; there is no path to substitute.\n\n### Step 4.5 - Graph health check (read-only integrity gate)\n\nA non-destructive diagnostic on the extraction, before labeling. It surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints, and self-loops — the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches. Read-only; never aborts.\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom graphify.diagnostics import diagnose_extraction, format_diagnostic_report\n\nextraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\nsummary = diagnose_extraction(extraction, directed=IS_DIRECTED, root=INPUT_PATH)\nprint(format_diagnostic_report(summary))\nflags = [f'{summary[k]} {label}' for k, label in (\n    ('dangling_endpoint_edges', 'dangling-endpoint edges'),\n    ('missing_endpoint_edges', 'missing-endpoint edges'),\n    ('self_loop_edges', 'self-loop edges'),\n    ('directed_same_endpoint_collapsed_edges', 'collapsed (directed) edges'),\n    ('undirected_same_endpoint_collapsed_edges', 'collapsed (undirected) edges'),\n) if summary.get(k, 0)]\nprint('GRAPH HEALTH WARNING: ' + '; '.join(flags) + ' - graph may be incomplete/corrupt.' if flags else 'Graph health: OK (no dangling/missing/collapsed edges).')\n\"\n```\n\nSubstitute `IS_DIRECTED` as in Step 4 (INPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root`). If a `GRAPH HEALTH WARNING` prints, surface it in the final summary (do not abort — the graph is still usable, but the integrity issue must be visible, per the Honesty Rules).\n\n### Step 5 - Label communities\n\nRead `graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json`. For each community key, look at its node labels and write a 2-5 word plain-language name (e.g. \"Attention Mechanism\", \"Training Pipeline\", \"Data Loading\").\n\nThen regenerate the report and save the labels for the visualizer:\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfrom graphify.build import build_from_json\nfrom graphify.cluster import score_all\nfrom graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions\nfrom graphify.report import generate\nfrom graphify.export import to_json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nextraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\ndetection  = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nanalysis   = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\n\n# root= as in Step 4 / the --update runbook (#1361) — same base for node-key parity.\nG = build_from_json(extraction, root=INPUT_PATH, directed=IS_DIRECTED)\ncommunities = {int(k): v for k, v in analysis['communities'].items()}\ncohesion = {int(k): v for k, v in analysis['cohesion'].items()}\ntokens = {'input': extraction.get('input_tokens', 0), 'output': extraction.get('output_tokens', 0)}\n\n# LABELS - replace these with the names you chose above\nlabels = LABELS_DICT\n\n# Regenerate questions with real community labels (labels affect question phrasing)\nquestions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)\n\nreport = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, analysis['gods'], analysis['surprises'], detection, tokens, INPUT_PATH, suggested_questions=questions)\nPath('graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_labels.json').write_text(json.dumps({str(k): v for k, v in labels.items()}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\n# Re-export so graph.json nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490).\n# Same extraction as Step 4, so the #479 shrink-guard passes on node count;\n# if it still refuses, surface the guard message - do not force past it.\nwrote = to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json', community_labels=labels)\nif not wrote:\n    print('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json (existing graph has more nodes; #479).')\n    print('If this shrink is intentional (you deleted files), re-run a full build with --force.')\nprint('Report updated with community labels')\n\"\n```\n\nReplace `LABELS_DICT` with the actual dict you constructed (e.g. `{0: \"Attention Mechanism\", 1: \"Training Pipeline\"}`).\nINPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root`; there is no path to substitute.\n\n### Step 6 - Generate Obsidian vault (opt-in) + HTML\n\n**Generate HTML always** (unless `--no-viz`). **Obsidian vault only if `--obsidian` was explicitly given** — skip it otherwise, it generates one file per node.\n\nIf `--obsidian` was given:\n\n- If `--obsidian-dir <path>` was also given, pass it via `--dir`. Otherwise defaults to `graphify-out/obsidian`.\n\n```bash\ngraphify export obsidian\n# or with custom dir: graphify export obsidian --dir ~/vaults/my-project\n```\n\nGenerate the HTML graph (always, unless `--no-viz`):\n\n```bash\ngraphify export html  # auto-aggregates to community view if graph > 5000 nodes\n# or: graphify export html --no-viz\n```\n\n### Steps 6b-8 - Wiki, Neo4j, FalkorDB, SVG, GraphML, MCP, benchmark (only on their flags)\n\nThese run only when their flag is present (`--wiki`, `--neo4j`/`--neo4j-push`, `--falkordb`/`--falkordb-push`, `--svg`, `--graphml`, `--mcp`) or, for the token-reduction benchmark, when `total_words` exceeds 5,000. A default run with no export flags skips all of them. See `references/exports.md` for each one. Run any `--wiki` export before Step 9 cleanup so `.graphify_labels.json` is still available.\n\n---\n\n### Step 9 - Save manifest, update cost tracker, clean up, and report\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom graphify.detect import save_manifest\n\n# Save manifest for --update\ndetect = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nextract = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\n# In --update mode, 'all_files' carries the full corpus; 'files' is the changed\n# subset. Full-rebuild mode populates only 'files', so the fallback handles that.\n# root= relativizes the manifest keys to the scan root (same base as the build),\n# so the on-disk manifest is portable across clones/machines and a later --update\n# matches cached files instead of missing every one (#1417).\n#\n# Only stamp semantic files (docs/papers/images) that ACTUALLY produced output:\n# a detected file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the\n# next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost\n# forever (#2015). This mirrors the library extract path exactly\n# (cli._stamped_manifest_files + clear_semantic + scan_corpus); do not stamp the\n# raw corpus. Code files are always stamped (AST is deterministic); only semantic\n# types are gated on output.\nfrom graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files\n_corpus = detect.get('all_files') or detect['files']\n# A file a subagent only partly read DID produce output, so the stamp filter alone would\n# keep it - but its node set covers just the head of the file, and stamping it means\n# detect_incremental reads it as done and never re-queues it, leaving the truncated graph\n# live forever. Name those files so they stay unstamped and are retried next run (#2225).\n_pf = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt')\n_partial = {l.strip() for l in _pf.read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\").splitlines() if l.strip()} if _pf.exists() else set()\n_manifest_files = _stamped_manifest_files(_corpus, extract, Path(INPUT_PATH), partial_source_files=_partial)\n# Files dispatched this run (the changed subset) but NOT stamped above still carry\n# a stale semantic_hash from a prior run; clear it so detect_incremental re-queues\n# them instead of reading them as unchanged (#1948).\n_sem_types = ('document', 'paper', 'image')\n_dispatched = {f for t, fl in detect['files'].items() if t in _sem_types for f in fl}\n_stamped = {f for fl in _manifest_files.values() for f in fl}\n_cleared = _dispatched - _stamped\n# scan_corpus = the RAW full corpus (not the stamp-filtered subset) so in-root\n# files newly excluded since last run are dropped rather than masquerading as\n# deletions; untouched files' prior rows are still preserved (#1908).\n_scan = {f for fl in _corpus.values() for f in fl}\nsave_manifest(_manifest_files, root=INPUT_PATH, scan_corpus=_scan, clear_semantic=_cleared or None)\n\n# Update cumulative cost tracker\ninput_tok = extract.get('input_tokens', 0)\noutput_tok = extract.get('output_tokens', 0)\n\ncost_path = Path('graphify-out/cost.json')\nif cost_path.exists():\n    cost = json.loads(cost_path.read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nelse:\n    cost = {'runs': [], 'total_input_tokens': 0, 'total_output_tokens': 0}\n\ncost['runs'].append({\n    'date': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),\n    'input_tokens': input_tok,\n    'output_tokens': output_tok,\n    'files': detect.get('total_files', 0),\n})\ncost['total_input_tokens'] += input_tok\ncost['total_output_tokens'] += output_tok\ncost_path.write_text(json.dumps(cost, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\n\nprint(f'This run: {input_tok:,} input tokens, {output_tok:,} output tokens')\nprint(f'All time: {cost[\\\"total_input_tokens\\\"]:,} input, {cost[\\\"total_output_tokens\\\"]:,} output ({len(cost[\\\"runs\\\"])} runs)')\n\"\nrm -f graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt\nfind graphify-out -maxdepth 1 -name '.graphify_chunk_*.json' -delete 2>/dev/null\nrm -f graphify-out/.needs_update 2>/dev/null || true\n```\n\nINPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root` (the scan root Steps 4-5 used), so the manifest is relativized to the scan root.\n\nTell the user (omit the obsidian line unless --obsidian was given):\n```\nGraph complete. Outputs in PATH_TO_DIR/graphify-out/\n\n  graph.html            - interactive graph, open in browser\n  GRAPH_REPORT.md       - audit report\n  graph.json            - raw graph data\n  obsidian/             - Obsidian vault (only if --obsidian was given)\n```\n\nIf graphify saved you time, consider supporting it: https://github.com/sponsors/safishamsi\n\nReplace PATH_TO_DIR with the actual absolute path of the directory that was processed.\n\nIf PATH_TO_DIR is inside a git repository, add one line to the report: `graphify-out/` was written into the working tree, so unless the repository already ignores it, it will show in `git status`; the user can add `graphify-out/` to `.gitignore`, or commit only the outputs their team should share (see https://docs.graphify.com/guides/team-workflows).\n\nThen paste these sections from GRAPH_REPORT.md directly into the chat:\n- God Nodes\n- Surprising Connections\n- Suggested Questions\n\nDo NOT paste the full report - just those three sections. Keep it concise.\n\nThen immediately offer to explore. Pick the single most interesting suggested question from the report - the one that crosses the most community boundaries or has the most surprising bridge node - and ask:\n\n> \"The most interesting question this graph can answer: **[question]**. Want me to trace it?\"\n\nIf the user says yes, run `/graphify query \"[question]\"` on the graph and walk them through the answer using the graph structure - which nodes connect, which community boundaries get crossed, what the path reveals. Your job after the pipeline is to be the guide.\n\n---\n\n## Interpreter guard for subcommands\n\nBefore running any subcommand below (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, `query`, `path`, `explain`, `add`), check that `.graphify_python` exists. If it's missing (e.g. user deleted `graphify-out/`), re-resolve the interpreter first:\n\n```bash\nif [ ! -f graphify-out/.graphify_python ]; then\n    GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)\n    if [ -n \"$GRAPHIFY_BIN\" ]; then\n        PYTHON=$(head -1 \"$GRAPHIFY_BIN\" | tr -d '#!')\n        case \"$PYTHON\" in *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) PYTHON=\"python3\" ;; esac\n    else\n        PYTHON=\"python3\"\n    fi\n    mkdir -p graphify-out\n    \"$PYTHON\" -c \"import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)\"\nfi\n```\n\n## For --update and --cluster-only\n\nBoth are non-default subcommands. `--update` re-extracts only new or changed files; `--cluster-only` reruns clustering on the existing graph. See `references/update.md` for both flows.\n\n---\n\n## For /graphify query\n\nWhen `graphify-out/graph.json` already exists and the user asks a question about the corpus, answer from the graph rather than rebuilding it:\n\n```bash\ngraphify query \"<question>\"\n```\n\nBefore traversal, expand the question against the graph's own vocabulary so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise. If the `graphify query` CLI is unavailable, fall back to an inline NetworkX traversal of `graphify-out/graph.json`. Answer using only what the graph output contains, and quote `source_location` when citing a specific fact. The nodes already extracted for those files are kept - they are still true - but the file is cached as partial and left unstamped in the manifest below, so the next `--update` re-dispatches it and replace-on-re-extract swaps the partial node set for a complete one. This is the same mechanism the library path uses for a truncated LLM response (#933, #1950), so both paths now recover instead of silently keeping a half-read file forever. A dispatched file with no coverage entry, or 0, was never opened, so whatever its chunk holds for it was guessed from its name: those items are dropped and the file is flagged the same way (#2225).\n\nMerge all chunk files into `.graphify_semantic_new.json`. **After each Agent call completes, read the real token counts from the Agent tool result's `usage` field and write them back into the chunk JSON before merging** — the chunk JSON itself always has placeholder zeros. Then run:\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json, glob\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nchunks = sorted(glob.glob('graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json'))\nall_nodes, all_edges, all_hyperedges = [], [], []\ntotal_in, total_out = 0, 0\nfor c in chunks:\n    d = json.loads(Path(c).read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\n    all_nodes += d.get('nodes', [])\n    all_edges += d.get('edges', [])\n    all_hyperedges += d.get('hyperedges', [])\n    total_in += d.get('input_tokens', 0)\n    total_out += d.get('output_tokens', 0)\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').write_text(json.dumps({\n    'nodes': all_nodes, 'edges': all_edges, 'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,\n    'input_tokens': total_in, 'output_tokens': total_out,\n}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nprint(f'Merged {len(chunks)} chunks: {total_in:,} in / {total_out:,} out tokens')\n\"\n```\n\nSave new results to cache. Pass the same SPEC_PATH as Step B0 — it stamps each entry with the prompt that produced it, and a write under a different prompt than the read lands where the next run won't look (#1939):\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom graphify.cache import save_semantic_cache\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nnew = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}\nuncached = [line for line in Path('graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\").splitlines() if line]\n# A partly-read file is cached with partial: True, which load_cached treats as a MISS,\n# so the next --update re-dispatches it instead of serving a truncated extraction forever\n# (#2225). Same contract the library path uses for a truncated LLM response (#933/#1950).\npartial = [line for line in Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\").splitlines() if line] if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').exists() else []\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\nsaved = save_semantic_cache(new.get('nodes', []), new.get('edges', []), new.get('hyperedges', []), root=INPUT_PATH, allowed_source_files=uncached, prompt_file='SPEC_PATH', partial_source_files=partial)\nnote = f' ({len(partial)} left partial for retry)' if partial else ''\nprint(f'Cached {saved} files' + note)\n\"\n```\n\nMerge cached + new results into `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json`:\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\ncached = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}\nnew = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}\n\nall_nodes = cached['nodes'] + new.get('nodes', [])\nall_edges = cached['edges'] + new.get('edges', [])\nall_hyperedges = cached.get('hyperedges', []) + new.get('hyperedges', [])\nseen = set()\ndeduped = []\nfor n in all_nodes:\n    if n['id'] not in seen:\n        seen.add(n['id'])\n        deduped.append(n)\n\nmerged = {\n    'nodes': deduped,\n    'edges': all_edges,\n    'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,\n    'input_tokens': new.get('input_tokens', 0),\n    'output_tokens': new.get('output_tokens', 0),\n}\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nprint(f'Extraction complete - {len(deduped)} nodes, {len(all_edges)} edges ({len(cached[\\\"nodes\\\"])} from cache, {len(new.get(\\\"nodes\\\",[]))} new)')\n\"\n```\nClean up temp files: `rm -f graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json`\n\n#### Part C - Merge AST + semantic into final extraction\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nast = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nsem = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\n\n# Stamp tier provenance on the semantic side. build._is_ast_tier reads\n# _origin when present and otherwise guesses from the SHAPE of\n# source_location ('L<line>' means AST). A subagent that writes 'L12' for a\n# doc section therefore made that node read as AST, and the next\n# graphify update deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it\n# seemed to belong to (#2843). extract() stamps its own items 'ast'; the\n# semantic side must say so explicitly.\nfor n in sem['nodes']:\n    n.setdefault('_origin', 'semantic')\nfor e in sem['edges']:\n    e.setdefault('_origin', 'semantic')\n\n# Merge: AST nodes first, semantic nodes deduplicated by id\nseen = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}\nmerged_nodes = list(ast['nodes'])\nfor n in sem['nodes']:\n    if n['id'] not in seen:\n        merged_nodes.append(n)\n        seen.add(n['id'])\n\nmerged_edges = ast['edges'] + sem['edges']\nmerged_hyperedges = sem.get('hyperedges', [])\nmerged = {\n    'nodes': merged_nodes,\n    'edges': merged_edges,\n    'hyperedges': merged_hyperedges,\n    'input_tokens': sem.get('input_tokens', 0),\n    'output_tokens': sem.get('output_tokens', 0),\n}\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\ntotal = len(merged_nodes)\nedges = len(merged_edges)\nprint(f'Merged: {total} nodes, {edges} edges ({len(ast[\\\"nodes\\\"])} AST + {len(sem[\\\"nodes\\\"])} semantic)')\n\"\n```\n\n### Step 4 - Build graph, cluster, analyze, generate outputs\n\n**Before starting:** the code blocks below pass `directed=IS_DIRECTED` to `build_from_json()` and `force=IS_FORCE` to `to_json()`. Replace `IS_DIRECTED` with `True` if `--directed` was given (builds a `DiGraph` preserving edge direction source→target), otherwise `False` (the default undirected `Graph`). Replace `IS_FORCE` with `True` if `--force` was given (permits intentional shrink, e.g. after deleting files), otherwise `False`. Substitute both so no literal `IS_DIRECTED` or `IS_FORCE` is left in the code. INPUT_PATH is not substituted — each block reads the scan root from the trusted `graphify-out/.graphify_root` that Step 1 resolved.\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p graphify-out\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfrom graphify.build import build_from_json\nfrom graphify.cluster import cluster, score_all\nfrom graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions\nfrom graphify.report import generate\nfrom graphify.export import to_json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nextraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\ndetection  = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\n\n# root= mirrors the --update runbook (#1361): relativize source_file to the same\n# base so the full build and incremental --update never drift apart on re-extract.\nG = build_from_json(extraction, root=INPUT_PATH, directed=IS_DIRECTED)\n# Guard BEFORE any write: an empty extraction must not clobber a good graph.json /\n# GRAPH_REPORT.md / analysis sidecar. Check immediately after build (#1392).\nif G.number_of_nodes() == 0:\n    print('ERROR: Graph is empty - extraction produced no nodes.')\n    print('Possible causes: all files were skipped, binary-only corpus, or extraction failed.')\n    raise SystemExit(1)\ncommunities = cluster(G)\ncohesion = score_all(G, communities)\ntokens = {'input': extraction.get('input_tokens', 0), 'output': extraction.get('output_tokens', 0)}\ngods = god_nodes(G)\nsurprises = surprising_connections(G, communities)\nlabels = {cid: 'Community ' + str(cid) for cid in communities}\n# Placeholder questions - regenerated with real labels in Step 5\nquestions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)\n\n# Export FIRST and honor the #479 shrink-guard: to_json returns False (writing\n# nothing) when the new graph is smaller than the existing graph.json. Only write\n# GRAPH_REPORT.md + the analysis sidecar when the graph was actually written, so\n# they never describe a graph that graph.json doesn't contain (#1392).\nwrote = to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json', force=IS_FORCE)\nif not wrote:\n    print('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json (existing graph has more nodes; #479).')\n    print('If this shrink is intentional (you deleted files), re-run a full build with --force.')\n    raise SystemExit(1)\nreport = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, gods, surprises, detection, tokens, INPUT_PATH, suggested_questions=questions)\nPath('graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nanalysis = {\n    'communities': {str(k): v for k, v in communities.items()},\n    'cohesion': {str(k): v for k, v in cohesion.items()},\n    'gods': gods,\n    'surprises': surprises,\n    'questions': questions,\n}\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json').write_text(json.dumps(analysis, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nprint(f'Graph: {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {G.number_of_edges()} edges, {len(communities)} communities')\n\"\n```\n\nIf this step prints `ERROR: Graph is empty`, stop and tell the user what happened - do not proceed to labeling or visualization.\n\nINPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root`; there is no path to substitute.\n\n### Step 4.5 - Graph health check (read-only integrity gate)\n\nA non-destructive diagnostic on the extraction, before labeling. It surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints, and self-loops — the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches. Read-only; never aborts.\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom graphify.diagnostics import diagnose_extraction, format_diagnostic_report\n\nextraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\nsummary = diagnose_extraction(extraction, directed=IS_DIRECTED, root=INPUT_PATH)\nprint(format_diagnostic_report(summary))\nflags = [f'{summary[k]} {label}' for k, label in (\n    ('dangling_endpoint_edges', 'dangling-endpoint edges'),\n    ('missing_endpoint_edges', 'missing-endpoint edges'),\n    ('self_loop_edges', 'self-loop edges'),\n    ('directed_same_endpoint_collapsed_edges', 'collapsed (directed) edges'),\n    ('undirected_same_endpoint_collapsed_edges', 'collapsed (undirected) edges'),\n) if summary.get(k, 0)]\nprint('GRAPH HEALTH WARNING: ' + '; '.join(flags) + ' - graph may be incomplete/corrupt.' if flags else 'Graph health: OK (no dangling/missing/collapsed edges).')\n\"\n```\n\nSubstitute `IS_DIRECTED` as in Step 4 (INPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root`). If a `GRAPH HEALTH WARNING` prints, surface it in the final summary (do not abort — the graph is still usable, but the integrity issue must be visible, per the Honesty Rules).\n\n### Step 5 - Label communities\n\nRead `graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json`. For each community key, look at its node labels and write a 2-5 word plain-language name (e.g. \"Attention Mechanism\", \"Training Pipeline\", \"Data Loading\").\n\nThen regenerate the report and save the labels for the visualizer:\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfrom graphify.build import build_from_json\nfrom graphify.cluster import score_all\nfrom graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions\nfrom graphify.report import generate\nfrom graphify.export import to_json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nextraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\ndetection  = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nanalysis   = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\n\n# root= as in Step 4 / the --update runbook (#1361) — same base for node-key parity.\nG = build_from_json(extraction, root=INPUT_PATH, directed=IS_DIRECTED)\ncommunities = {int(k): v for k, v in analysis['communities'].items()}\ncohesion = {int(k): v for k, v in analysis['cohesion'].items()}\ntokens = {'input': extraction.get('input_tokens', 0), 'output': extraction.get('output_tokens', 0)}\n\n# LABELS - replace these with the names you chose above\nlabels = LABELS_DICT\n\n# Regenerate questions with real community labels (labels affect question phrasing)\nquestions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)\n\nreport = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, analysis['gods'], analysis['surprises'], detection, tokens, INPUT_PATH, suggested_questions=questions)\nPath('graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\nPath('graphify-out/.graphify_labels.json').write_text(json.dumps({str(k): v for k, v in labels.items()}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\n# Re-export so graph.json nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490).\n# Same extraction as Step 4, so the #479 shrink-guard passes on node count;\n# if it still refuses, surface the guard message - do not force past it.\nwrote = to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json', community_labels=labels)\nif not wrote:\n    print('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json (existing graph has more nodes; #479).')\n    print('If this shrink is intentional (you deleted files), re-run a full build with --force.')\nprint('Report updated with community labels')\n\"\n```\n\nReplace `LABELS_DICT` with the actual dict you constructed (e.g. `{0: \"Attention Mechanism\", 1: \"Training Pipeline\"}`).\nINPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root`; there is no path to substitute.\n\n### Step 6 - Generate Obsidian vault (opt-in) + HTML\n\n**Generate HTML always** (unless `--no-viz`). **Obsidian vault only if `--obsidian` was explicitly given** — skip it otherwise, it generates one file per node.\n\nIf `--obsidian` was given:\n\n- If `--obsidian-dir <path>` was also given, pass it via `--dir`. Run any `--wiki` export before Step 9 cleanup so `.graphify_labels.json` is still available.\n\n---\n\n### Step 9 - Save manifest, update cost tracker, clean up, and report\n\n```bash\n$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c \"\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom graphify.detect import save_manifest\n\n# Save manifest for --update\ndetect = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nextract = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nINPUT_PATH = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8-sig\\\").strip()\n# In --update mode, 'all_files' carries the full corpus; 'files' is the changed\n# subset. Full-rebuild mode populates only 'files', so the fallback handles that.\n# root= relativizes the manifest keys to the scan root (same base as the build),\n# so the on-disk manifest is portable across clones/machines and a later --update\n# matches cached files instead of missing every one (#1417).\n#\n# Only stamp semantic files (docs/papers/images) that ACTUALLY produced output:\n# a detected file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the\n# next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost\n# forever (#2015). This mirrors the library extract path exactly\n# (cli._stamped_manifest_files + clear_semantic + scan_corpus); do not stamp the\n# raw corpus. Code files are always stamped (AST is deterministic); only semantic\n# types are gated on output.\nfrom graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files\n_corpus = detect.get('all_files') or detect['files']\n# A file a subagent only partly read DID produce output, so the stamp filter alone would\n# keep it - but its node set covers just the head of the file, and stamping it means\n# detect_incremental reads it as done and never re-queues it, leaving the truncated graph\n# live forever. Name those files so they stay unstamped and are retried next run (#2225).\n_pf = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt')\n_partial = {l.strip() for l in _pf.read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\").splitlines() if l.strip()} if _pf.exists() else set()\n_manifest_files = _stamped_manifest_files(_corpus, extract, Path(INPUT_PATH), partial_source_files=_partial)\n# Files dispatched this run (the changed subset) but NOT stamped above still carry\n# a stale semantic_hash from a prior run; clear it so detect_incremental re-queues\n# them instead of reading them as unchanged (#1948).\n_sem_types = ('document', 'paper', 'image')\n_dispatched = {f for t, fl in detect['files'].items() if t in _sem_types for f in fl}\n_stamped = {f for fl in _manifest_files.values() for f in fl}\n_cleared = _dispatched - _stamped\n# scan_corpus = the RAW full corpus (not the stamp-filtered subset) so in-root\n# files newly excluded since last run are dropped rather than masquerading as\n# deletions; untouched files' prior rows are still preserved (#1908).\n_scan = {f for fl in _corpus.values() for f in fl}\nsave_manifest(_manifest_files, root=INPUT_PATH, scan_corpus=_scan, clear_semantic=_cleared or None)\n\n# Update cumulative cost tracker\ninput_tok = extract.get('input_tokens', 0)\noutput_tok = extract.get('output_tokens', 0)\n\ncost_path = Path('graphify-out/cost.json')\nif cost_path.exists():\n    cost = json.loads(cost_path.read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\nelse:\n    cost = {'runs': [], 'total_input_tokens': 0, 'total_output_tokens': 0}\n\ncost['runs'].append({\n    'date': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),\n    'input_tokens': input_tok,\n    'output_tokens': output_tok,\n    'files': detect.get('total_files', 0),\n})\ncost['total_input_tokens'] += input_tok\ncost['total_output_tokens'] += output_tok\ncost_path.write_text(json.dumps(cost, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\n\nprint(f'This run: {input_tok:,} input tokens, {output_tok:,} output tokens')\nprint(f'All time: {cost[\\\"total_input_tokens\\\"]:,} input, {cost[\\\"total_output_tokens\\\"]:,} output ({len(cost[\\\"runs\\\"])} runs)')\n\"\nrm -f graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt\nfind graphify-out -maxdepth 1 -name '.graphify_chunk_*.json' -delete 2>/dev/null\nrm -f graphify-out/.needs_update 2>/dev/null || true\n```\n\nINPUT_PATH is read from `graphify-out/.graphify_root` (the scan root Steps 4-5 used), so the manifest is relativized to the scan root.\n\nTell the user (omit the obsidian line unless --obsidian was given):\n```\nGraph complete. Outputs in PATH_TO_DIR/graphify-out/\n\n  graph.html            - interactive graph, open in browser\n  GRAPH_REPORT.md       - audit report\n  graph.json            - raw graph data\n  obsidian/             - Obsidian vault (only if --obsidian was given)\n```\n\nIf graphify saved you time, consider supporting it: https://github.com/sponsors/safishamsi\n\nReplace PATH_TO_DIR with the actual absolute path of the directory that was processed.\n\nIf PATH_TO_DIR is inside a git repository, add one line to the report: `graphify-out/` was written into the working tree, so unless the repository already ignores it, it will show in `git status`; the user can add `graphify-out/` to `.gitignore`, or commit only the outputs their team should share (see https://docs.graphify.com/guides/team-workflows).\n\nThen paste these sections from GRAPH_REPORT.md directly into the chat:\n- God Nodes\n- Surprising Connections\n- Suggested Questions\n\nDo NOT paste the full report - just those three sections. Keep it concise.\n\nThen immediately offer to explore. Pick the single most interesting suggested question from the report - the one that crosses the most community boundaries or has the most surprising bridge node - and ask:\n\n> \"The most interesting question this graph can answer: **[question]**. Want me to trace it?\"\n\nIf the user says yes, run `/graphify query \"[question]\"` on the graph and walk them through the answer using the graph structure - which nodes connect, which community boundaries get crossed, what the path reveals. Your job after the pipeline is to be the guide.\n\n---\n\n## Interpreter guard for subcommands\n\nBefore running any subcommand below (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, `query`, `path`, `explain`, `add`), check that `.graphify_python` exists. If it's missing (e.g. user deleted `graphify-out/`), re-resolve the interpreter first:\n\n```bash\nif [ ! -f graphify-out/.graphify_python ]; then\n    GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)\n    if [ -n \"$GRAPHIFY_BIN\" ]; then\n        PYTHON=$(head -1 \"$GRAPHIFY_BIN\" | tr -d '#!')\n        case \"$PYTHON\" in *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) PYTHON=\"python3\" ;; esac\n    else\n        PYTHON=\"python3\"\n    fi\n    mkdir -p graphify-out\n    \"$PYTHON\" -c \"import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)\"\nfi\n```\n\n## For --update and --cluster-only\n\nBoth are non-default subcommands. `--update` re-extracts only new or changed files; `--cluster-only` reruns clustering on the existing graph. See `references/update.md` for both flows.\n\n---\n\n## For /graphify query\n\nWhen `graphify-out/graph.json` already exists and the user asks a question about the corpus, answer from the graph rather than rebuilding it:\n\n```bash\ngraphify query \"<question>\"\n```\n\nBefore traversal, expand the question against the graph's own vocabulary so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise. If the `graphify query` CLI is unavailable, fall back to an inline NetworkX traversal of `graphify-out/graph.json`. Answer using only what the graph output contains, and quote `source_location` when citing a specific fact. For that vocab-expansion step, the BFS/DFS traversal modes, the `--budget` cap, the NetworkX fallback, `save-result` feedback, and the `/graphify path` and `/graphify explain` flows, see `references/query.md`.\n\n---\n\n## For /graphify add and --watch\n\nNeither is part of the default build. Based on Emil Kowalski's \"Animations on the Web\" course.\n---\n\n# Next.js Animations\n\n## Overview\n\nThis skill provides comprehensive guidance for implementing smooth, performant, and accessible animations in Next.js and React applications. It covers CSS animations, Framer Motion, easing principles, and accessibility considerations.\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Easing Cheat Sheet\n\n| Animation Type | Easing | Duration |\n|----------------|--------|----------|\n| Element entering | `ease-out` | 200-300ms |\n| Element moving on screen | `ease-in-out` | 200-300ms |\n| Element exiting | `ease-in` | 150-200ms |\n| Hover effects | `ease` | 150ms |\n| Opacity only | `linear` | varies |\n\n### Canonical Timing Table\n\n| Motion type | Duration | Easing |\n|---|---|---|\n| Micro interaction (hover, focus) | 120-220ms | ease-out |\n| UI state transition (modal, dropdown) | 180-320ms | ease-in-out |\n| Entrance reveal (scroll-triggered) | 240-420ms | ease-out |\n| Large cinematic (pinned scene) | 400-800ms | custom, justified |\n\nThis table is the canonical motion timing reference. Other skills (scroll-choreography, design-md, taste-skill) align with these ranges.\n\n### CSS Custom Properties (Recommended)\n\n```css\n:root {\n  --ease-out-quint: cubic-bezier(.23, 1, .32, 1);\n  --ease-in-out-cubic: cubic-bezier(.645, .045, .355, 1);\n  --ease-out-cubic: cubic-bezier(.33, 1, .68, 1);\n}\n```\n\n## Common Animation Patterns\n\n### 1. Hover Lift Effect\n\n```css\n.card {\n  transition: transform 200ms var(--ease-out-quint),\n              box-shadow 200ms var(--ease-out-quint);\n}\n.card:hover {\n  transform: translateY(-4px);\n  box-shadow: 0 12px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15);\n}\n```\n\n### 2. Button Press\n\n```css\n.button {\n  transition: transform 100ms ease-out;\n}\n.button:active {\n  transform: scale(0.97);\n}\n```\n\n### 3. Fade In on Mount (Framer Motion)\n\n```tsx\n<motion.div\n  initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}\n  animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}\n  transition={{ duration: 0.3, ease: [.23, 1, .32, 1] }}\n>\n  Content\n</motion.div>\n```\n\n### 4. Modal with Exit Animation\n\n```tsx\n<AnimatePresence>\n  {isOpen && (\n    <motion.div\n      initial={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 }}\n      animate={{ opacity: 1, scale: 1 }}\n      exit={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 }}\n      transition={{ duration: 0.2, ease: \"easeOut\" }}\n    >\n      {children}\n    </motion.div>\n  )}\n</AnimatePresence>\n```\n\n### 5. Tab Indicator (Shared Layout)\n\n```tsx\n{tabs.map(tab => (\n  <button key={tab} onClick={() => setActive(tab)} className=\"relative px-4 py-2\">\n    {tab}\n    {active === tab && (\n      <motion.div\n        layoutId=\"tab-indicator\"\n        className=\"absolute inset-0 bg-blue-500 rounded -z-10\"\n        transition={{ type: \"spring\", stiffness: 400, damping: 30 }}\n      />\n    )}\n  </button>\n))}\n```\n\n### 6. Staggered List Animation\n\n```tsx\nconst container = {\n  hidden: { opacity: 0 },\n  visible: {\n    opacity: 1,\n    transition: { staggerChildren: 0.1 }\n  }\n}\n\nconst item = {\n  hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 20 },\n  visible: { opacity: 1, y: 0 }\n}\n\n<motion.ul variants={container} initial=\"hidden\" animate=\"visible\">\n  {items.map(i => <motion.li key={i} variants={item}>{i}</motion.li>)}\n</motion.ul>\n```\n\n## Golden Rules\n\n1. **Exits faster than enters**: Exit animations should be ~75% of enter duration\n2. **Only animate transform and opacity**: These are GPU-accelerated\n3. **200-300ms is the sweet spot**: Most animations should be in this range\n4. **Always respect prefers-reduced-motion**: See accessibility section in references\n5. **Use springs for interruptible animations**: Better UX when users interrupt\n\n## Reusable Patterns\n\nUse the inline patterns above as the source of truth. The installed skill includes `references/` documents, but not a guaranteed `examples/` directory. Do not stop to look for missing example files.\n\nBefore adding animation code to a component, choose one pattern:\n\n| Pattern | Use for | Avoid when |\n|---------|---------|------------|\n| Fade-up reveal | Section entrances | Every tiny child element |\n| Staggered list | Cards, logos, feature lists | Large paragraphs |\n| Scroll-linked transform | Storytelling, hero depth | Core text readability |\n| Shared layout | Tabs, nav indicators | Pure decoration |\n| CSS hover transition | Buttons/cards | Complex state changes |\n\n## References\n\nFor detailed documentation, read the reference files:\n\n- `references/easing-and-timing.md` - Easing functions, timing guidelines, spring configuration\n- `references/css-animations.md` - Transforms, transitions, keyframes, clip-path\n- `references/framer-motion.md` - Motion components, AnimatePresence, variants, layout animations, hooks\n- `references/performance-accessibility.md` - 60fps optimization, prefers-reduced-motion, accessibility\n\n## When to Use What\n\n| Scenario | Recommended Approach |\n|----------|---------------------|\n| Simple hover effects | CSS transitions |\n| Enter/exit animations | Motion v12 + AnimatePresence |\n| Layout changes | Motion `layout` prop |\n| Shared element transitions | Motion `layoutId` |\n| Scroll-linked animations | Motion `scroll()` (native ScrollTimeline) |\n| Complex orchestrated animations | Motion variants |\n| Drag interactions | Motion drag gestures |\n| Scroll-pin / horizontal-pan | GSAP ScrollTrigger (for advanced scrub/pin) |\n| Performance-critical | CSS-only with transforms |\n## Dependencies\n\nFor Motion v12 (preferred):\n```bash\nnpm install motion\n```\n\nFor legacy Framer Motion projects:\n```bash\npnpm add framer-motion react-use-measure usehooks-ts\n```\n\n## Motion v12 — Production-Grade Library (Preferred)\n\n**motion.dev** (v12, prev. Modal with Exit Animation\n\n```tsx\n<AnimatePresence>\n  {isOpen && (\n    <motion.div\n      initial={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 }}\n      animate={{ opacity: 1, scale: 1 }}\n      exit={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 }}\n      transition={{ duration: 0.2, ease: \"easeOut\" }}\n    >\n      {children}\n    </motion.div>\n  )}\n</AnimatePresence>\n```\n\n### 5. Tab Indicator (Shared Layout)\n\n```tsx\n{tabs.map(tab => (\n  <button key={tab} onClick={() => setActive(tab)} className=\"relative px-4 py-2\">\n    {tab}\n    {active === tab && (\n      <motion.div\n        layoutId=\"tab-indicator\"\n        className=\"absolute inset-0 bg-blue-500 rounded -z-10\"\n        transition={{ type: \"spring\", stiffness: 400, damping: 30 }}\n      />\n    )}\n  </button>\n))}\n```\n\n### 6. Staggered List Animation\n\n```tsx\nconst container = {\n  hidden: { opacity: 0 },\n  visible: {\n    opacity: 1,\n    transition: { staggerChildren: 0.1 }\n  }\n}\n\nconst item = {\n  hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 20 },\n  visible: { opacity: 1, y: 0 }\n}\n\n<motion.ul variants={container} initial=\"hidden\" animate=\"visible\">\n  {items.map(i => <motion.li key={i} variants={item}>{i}</motion.li>)}\n</motion.ul>\n```\n\n## Golden Rules\n\n1. **Exits faster than enters**: Exit animations should be ~75% of enter duration\n2. **Only animate transform and opacity**: These are GPU-accelerated\n3. **200-300ms is the sweet spot**: Most animations should be in this range\n4. **Always respect prefers-reduced-motion**: See accessibility section in references\n5. **Use springs for interruptible animations**: Better UX when users interrupt\n\n## Reusable Patterns\n\nUse the inline patterns above as the source of truth. The installed skill includes `references/` documents, but not a guaranteed `examples/` directory. Do not stop to look for missing example files.\n\nBefore adding animation code to a component, choose one pattern:\n\n| Pattern | Use for | Avoid when |\n|---------|---------|------------|\n| Fade-up reveal | Section entrances | Every tiny child element |\n| Staggered list | Cards, logos, feature lists | Large paragraphs |\n| Scroll-linked transform | Storytelling, hero depth | Core text readability |\n| Shared layout | Tabs, nav indicators | Pure decoration |\n| CSS hover transition | Buttons/cards | Complex state changes |\n\n## References\n\nFor detailed documentation, read the reference files:\n\n- `references/easing-and-timing.md` - Easing functions, timing guidelines, spring configuration\n- `references/css-animations.md` - Transforms, transitions, keyframes, clip-path\n- `references/framer-motion.md` - Motion components, AnimatePresence, variants, layout animations, hooks\n- `references/performance-accessibility.md` - 60fps optimization, prefers-reduced-motion, accessibility\n\n## When to Use What\n\n| Scenario | Recommended Approach |\n|----------|---------------------|\n| Simple hover effects | CSS transitions |\n| Enter/exit animations | Motion v12 + AnimatePresence |\n| Layout changes | Motion `layout` prop |\n| Shared element transitions | Motion `layoutId` |\n| Scroll-linked animations | Motion `scroll()` (native ScrollTimeline) |\n| Complex orchestrated animations | Motion variants |\n| Drag interactions | Motion drag gestures |\n| Scroll-pin / horizontal-pan | GSAP ScrollTrigger (for advanced scrub/pin) |\n| Performance-critical | CSS-only with transforms |\n## Dependencies\n\nFor Motion v12 (preferred):\n```bash\nnpm install motion\n```\n\nFor legacy Framer Motion projects:\n```bash\npnpm add framer-motion react-use-measure usehooks-ts\n```\n\n## Motion v12 — Production-Grade Library (Preferred)\n\n**motion.dev** (v12, prev. Framer Motion) is the recommended animation library.\nAll patterns above work with `motion/react` — same API (`motion.div`, `AnimatePresence`, `layoutId`, `useScroll`).\n\n### 400+ Copy-Paste Examples\n\nBrowse https://examples.motion.dev/react before writing custom animation code.\n\n| Pattern | Example URL |\n|---------|-------------|\n| Scroll velocity 3D planes | `examples.motion.dev/react/scroll-velocity-linked-offset` |\n| Typewriter text | `examples.motion.dev/react/typewriter` |\n| iOS-style folder expand | `examples.motion.dev/react/ios-app-folder` |\n| iOS pointer animation | `examples.motion.dev/react/ios-pointer` |\n| Skeleton shimmer | `examples.motion.dev/react/skeleton-shimmer` |\n| Floating action button | `examples.motion.dev/react/floating-action-button` |\n\n### API Differences from Framer Motion\n\n| Feature | Framer Motion (old) | Motion v12 (new) |\n|---------|--------------------|--------------------|\n| Package | `framer-motion` | `motion` |\n| React import | `import { motion } from \"framer-motion\"` | `import { motion } from \"motion/react\"` |\n| Bundle size | ~31 KB gzipped | ~5 KB gzipped (tree-shaken) |\n| Scroll-driven | `useScroll` | `scroll()` (native ScrollTimeline) |\n| Independent transforms | wrappers needed | native `x`, `y`, `rotate`, `scale` on same element |\n\n### Dependencies\n\n```bash\nnpm install motion\n# No peer deps. Добавить узкие средства проверки frontend\n+В `frontend/package.json` добавить devDependencies `vitest` версии `3.2.4` и `@playwright/test` версии `1.56.1`; scripts `\"test:unit\": \"vitest run\"` и `\"test:visual\": \"playwright test\"`. Выполнить `npm install --save-dev --save-exact vitest@3.2.4 @playwright/test@1.56.1` из `frontend/`. Создать `frontend/vitest.config.ts`: environment node, include `src/scene/**/*.test.ts`; отдельная конфигурация не меняет рабочий Vite. Создать `frontend/playwright.config.ts`: testDir `./tests`, один worker, headless Chromium, webServer `npm run dev -- --port 41736 --strictPort`, baseURL `http://127.0.0.1:41736`, `reuseExistingServer: false`, основной viewport 1080×1920. Выполнить `npx playwright install chromium`.\n+Существующего frontend test runner нет в прочитанном package.json; добавить его только для рискованных геометрических/анимационных контрактов. Не создавать тесты, проверяющие текст исходников или количество компонентов.\n+Проверка: `npm run build` из `frontend/` — прежнее приложение собирается. Готовность: lockfile фиксирует версии; frontend runtime ещё не менялся.\n+\n+### Шаг 2. Типизировать модельную идентичность и состояние сцены\n+В `frontend/src/types.ts` добавить `\"file\"` и data-поля из раздела контрактов; `data.lifecycle_known?: boolean` также типизировать. Создать `frontend/src/scene/types.ts`:\n+- `Point { x: number; y: number }`, `Viewport { width: number; height: number; dpr: number }`, `Camera { x: number; y: number; zoom: number }`.\n+- `NetworkScope = \"internet\" | \"lan\" | \"localhost\"`.\n+- `SceneNode { id: string; source: GraphNode; position: Point; layer: number; icon: string; label: string | null; radius: number }`.\n+- `SceneEdge { id: string; source: string; target: string; active: boolean; lastSeen: number }`.\n+- `SceneModel { at: number; nodes: SceneNode[]; edges: SceneEdge[]; bounds: { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number } }`.\n+- `SceneOptions { mode: ViewMode; search: string; statuses: Set<string>; selected: string | null; focus: boolean }`.\n+Проверка: `npm run build`. Готовность: старые Snapshot/Event JSON совместимы, нет требования новых полей у старой истории.\n+\n+### Шаг 3. Жизненный цикл и модельная идентичность в адаптерах\n+Точная таблица извлечения и проверки приведена в секции «Телеметрия» ниже; выполнить её перед изменением builder. Сохранить сигнатуры `OmpAdapter.parse(record, source, line_number)` и `CodexAdapter.parse(record, source, line_number)`, идентификаторы сессий и `JsonlAdapter.event(...)`. Добавить чистую функцию `normalize_model_provider(provider: str | None, model_id: str | None) -> str | None` в создаваемый `agent_atlas/identity.py`; не выводить провайдера только из runtime или обычного непрефиксного имени модели. Все новые события использовать при воспроизведении истории.\n+Проверка: `python -m pytest tests/test_adapters.py -q`. Готовность: последовательность prompt→tool→tool-result→final даёт active до final и idle после; метаданные не сохраняют текст ответа; неизвестные данные не создают логотип.\n+\n+### Шаг 4. Разделить подтверждённые файлы и директории\n+В `agent_atlas/adapters/base.py` добавить `extract_path_resources(value: Any, cwd: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, str]]`. Каждая запись имеет `path` и `path_kind` из `\"file\"`, `\"directory\"`, `\"unknown\"`. Для ключей `file`, `filename` — file; `directory`, `cwd`, `workdir` — directory; для `path`, `target` и regex-путей — unknown. Относительные файловые пути разрешать через cwd как существующий `extract_resources`. Не использовать наличие расширения как доказательство файла и не читать файловую систему для классификации истории.\n+Сохранить `extract_resources` как используемую функцию получения paths/urls. В payload `tool.started` обоих адаптеров добавить `path_resources`, сохранять `paths` для старых потребителей. Это не compatibility alias: `paths` по-прежнему общий список ресурсов, `path_resources` добавляет доказанный тип.\n+Для OMP полей `path` в инструментах `read`, `edit`, `write`, `apply_patch` и Codex patch-операций тип file определять только по явно файловой операции/строкам patch `*** Add File:`, `*** Update File:`, `*** Delete File:`; не парсить содержимое создаваемого файла. Не считать `read` каталога доказанным файлом: если нет явного файлового поля/patch, unknown.\n+Проверка: расширить `tests/test_adapters.py`: extensionless `filename` → file; directory с точкой → directory; неоднозначный `path` → unknown; относительный filename → cwd/filename; URL не попадает в пути. `python -m pytest tests/test_adapters.py -q`. Готовность: нет выдуманного файла по точке в имени.\n+\n+### Шаг 5. Историческое состояние без чтения всех tool events за семь дней каждый polling\n+В `agent_atlas/database.py` добавить `snapshot_events(self, end: float, resource_window: float = 300.0) -> list[Event]`. Существующий `events(start, end)` не менять. Новый SQL выбирает union по id:\n+1. все события с `end-resource_window <= ts <= end`;\n+2. для каждой пары `(provider, agent_id)` последнюю запись каждого kind из `session.started`, `agent.active`, `agent.idle`, `agent.error`, `agent.ended`, `agent.metadata`, `candidate.detected`, `process.sample` в диапазоне `[end-604800, end]`;\n+3. последнюю запись с payload.cwd не null для каждой такой пары в этом же диапазоне.\n+Использовать `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY provider, agent_id, kind ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC)` и аналогичный partition без kind для cwd; JSON-функцию `json_extract(payload,'$.cwd')`. Не `GROUP BY` с произвольными неагрегированными полями. Дедупликация по id, финальный порядок `(ts,id)`. Блокировку `_lock` брать как в `events`. Индекс `(provider, agent_id, kind, ts)` создать через существующий `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, без удаления БД. Повреждённые payload не ожидаются, поскольку пишет `Event.to_dict`; исключения SQLite не подавлять.\n+В `api.py:create_app.snapshot` заменить `database.events(end-300,end)` на `database.snapshot_events(end)`, сохранить передачу `end` и positions. Backend request shape не меняется.\n+Создать `tests/test_database.py`: при end=10000 вернуть final на 9300 и metadata на 9200, убрать ресурс на 9600, оставить ресурс на 9800; не брать события после end; пары с одинаковым agent_id и разным provider не смешивать. `python -m pytest tests/test_database.py tests/test_api.py -q`.\n+Готовность: сон на отметке >300 s воспроизводим, будущий final не влияет на прошлое, query не возвращает все старые tool events.\n+\n+### Шаг 6. Собирать семантические состояния, файлы и сетевые области\n+В `agent_atlas/graph.py:GraphBuilder.build` сохранить сигнатуру, убрать два принудительных пересчёта статуса по возрасту для агентов и фильтр `active_nodes` для агентов/проектов. Обычные process-only агенты с последним process.sample старше 300 s убрать, чтобы семь дней не оставляли давно исчезнувшие PID; lifecycle-сессии не удалять по PID. PID не использовать для слияния без достоверного session→process поля.\n+В ветке tool.started использовать path_resources: file → node `key(\"file\", normalized_path.casefold())`, kind `\"file\"`, data.path и path_kind; directory → folder; unknown → прежняя группировка `folder_for` и data.last_path, не отдельный файл. Старые paths без typed metadata продолжают показывать папки.\n+Создать `agent_atlas/network.py`, функция `classify_endpoint(value: str) -> str`: URL разбирать `urlparse`, endpoint принимать `host:port`, `[IPv6]:port`, голый host/IP. localhost/суффикс `.localhost`, IPv4 127/8 и IPv6 ::1 → localhost; RFC1918 10/8,172.16/12,192.168/16, IPv4 link-local169.254/16, IPv6 fc00/7,fe80/10, `.local` и одноуровневое имя → lan; всё остальное → internet. Не DNS lookup, не `is_private` для всего диапазона special-use, не считать неизвестный FQDN локальным. Пустое/неразбираемое значение → internet с исходной подписью, без падения.\n+В обеих сетевых ветках builder добавить data.network_scope на domain. Не создавать cloud-ноды backend: это оформление группы, а не новые сетевые сущности.\n+Проверка: `python -m pytest tests/test_graph.py tests/test_database.py tests/test_adapters.py tests/test_network.py -q`. Begin Patch\n[local://atlas-visual-plan.md#86B9]\nPUT >$:\n+\n+## Декомпозиция шага 11 для небольшой модели\n+Выполнять вместо попытки написать renderer целиком. Каждый подпункт — отдельная небольшая правка с проверкой; не создавать заглушки будущих методов.\n+\n+### 11a. Статические изометрические объекты\n+Создать `frontend/src/scene/paint.ts`: `drawNode(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, node: SceneNode, sprites: SpriteAtlas, motion: MotionSample): void` и `drawLabel(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, node: SceneNode): void`. Обе принимают world-coordinate context, ничего не знают о камере/input/RAF. drawNode рисует shadow, локальную transform вокруг position, спрайт, затем badge; фрагментирование error через четыре clip-rect спрайта. drawLabel горизонтальная после restore, полный текст сокращён как SceneNode.label. Кэш измерений текста — Map label→width, за пределами кадра.\n+Проверка: `npm run build`; `npm run test:unit`. Готовность: painter не создаёт RAF, не fetch-ит и не меняет model.\n+\n+### 11b. Слой мира и потоки\n+В paint.ts добавить `drawBackground(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, viewport: Viewport, elapsedMs: number, reducedMotion: boolean): void`, `drawClouds(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, model: SceneModel, sprites: SpriteAtlas): void`, `drawEdges(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, model: SceneModel, elapsedMs: number, selected: string | null, reducedMotion: boolean): void`. Background вызывается в screen-space, остальное world-space. drawClouds получает network scope через node.source.data и соответствующие bounds; drawEdges использует geometry helpers и cached id→node/curve. Не соединять домены друг с другом только ради облака.\n+Проверка: `npm run build`; `npm run test:unit -- src/scene/geometry.test.ts`. Готовность: три вида облаков/направленные curves готовы, но ещё не подключены к App.\n+\n+### 11c. Статический SceneRenderer и камера\n+Создать renderer.ts и реализовать constructor, setModel, resize, fit, focusNode, destroy только со статическим paint. Реальные drawNode/labels вызываются с sampleMotion(reducedMotion=true). Canvas transform: reset→DPR→background→camera transform→cloud/edges/nodes/labels. destroy уже освобождает собственные resources; никаких пустых методов setVisible/setReducedMotion до их реализации11f.\n+Проверка: `npm run build`; `npm run test:unit -- src/scene/geometry.test.ts src/scene/model.test.ts`. Готовность: статическая сцена воспроизводима на canvas без новой runtime-зависимости.\n+\n+### 11d. Взаимодействие без анимационного кода\n+Создать `frontend/src/scene/input.ts`: `bindSceneInput(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, handlers: InputHandlers): () => void`. `InputHandlers` имеет `getModel: () => SceneModel`, `getCamera: () => Camera`, `getViewport: () => Viewport`, `setCamera: (camera: Camera) => void`, `moveNode: (id: string, position: Point, commit: boolean) => void`, `select: (id: string | null) => void`, `hover: (id: string | null, point: Point | null) => void`, `fit: () => void`. Здесь только pointer/wheel/pinch с порогами из шага11; очистка возвращается bindSceneInput, вызов из renderer.destroy.\n+Проверка: `npm run build`; `npm run test:unit -- src/scene/geometry.test.ts`.
